label probe: one CREATE of up to 40 `(n<i>:_Entity:`<label>`)` patterns, RETURN elementId(n<i>) AS e<i> (two labels shown)
label probe cleanup: `MATCH (n<i>:`<label>`) WHERE elementId(n<i>) = $e<i>` per label joined with spaces, then `DELETE n0, n1, …`

queries.assembly_rule: write_candidate(entity): `_merge_entity_clause('s','s')` = MERGE (s:_Entity:<label> {_source_id: $s_key}) + _ENTITY_SET (ON CREATE SET … / SET updated_at) + SET name = coalesce(…), then RETURN elementId(s)
write_candidate(relation): subject clause + WITH s + object clause + WITH s, o + MERGE (s)-[r:<predicate>]->(o) with ON CREATE SET / SET, RETURN the three element ids
write_candidate(property): subject clause + SET s.`<prop>` = $value + RETURN elementId(s)
createDatasource: head `CREATE DATASOURCE <name> WITH ENGINE = '<engine>', PARAMETERS = ` + `{<k>: $<k>, …}` over the keys the form filled (password, or credentials when the keychain holds it)
alterCredentials without a keychain: head `ALTER DATASOURCE <name> SET CREDENTIALS = ` + '{user: $user, password: $password}'
alterCredentials with a keychain reference: head + '{user: $user, credentials: $credentials}'
nl2cypher is LLM-written; only the examples its prompt records: `(po:PurchaseOrder)-[:ORDERED_FROM]->(s:Supplier)` with every node labelled, `RETURN s.name AS supplier, …` named columns, `LIMIT 100`
nl2cypher prompt example: a label predicate in WHERE (`WHERE n:Label`, `NOT n:Label`)
